chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever recites one hundred verses, praying with them during a night, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will write for him, due to it, the Qunoot (supplication) for a night;
and whoever recites two hundred verses outside of prayer, the Quran will not argue against him on the Day of Judgment;
and whoever recites five hundred verses during a day and a night, in the prayer of the day and the night, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will write for him in the Guarded Tablet, a Qintar of good deeds;
and the Qintar is one thousand two hundred Owqiya, and the Owqiya is greater than the mountain of Uhud.

key_terms.أُوقِيَّة: A unit of weight/currency, described here as being greater than Mount Uhud in spiritual value.
key_terms.اللَّوْحِ الْمَحْفُوظِ: The Guarded Tablet, a celestial record where deeds are inscribed.
key_terms.قُنُوت: Supplication or standing in prayer, specifically referring to a special divine record of supplication for the reciter.
key_terms.قِنْطَار: A large unit of weight or currency used here to denote a massive quantity of good deeds.
key_terms.لَمْ يُحَاجَّهُ الْقُرْآنُ: The Quran will not argue against him; a state where the Quran serves as evidence for rather than against the person on Judgment Day.

ai.seo_question: What are the rewards for reciting 100, 200, or 500 verses of the Quran?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the cumulative spiritual merit of Quranic recitation, distinguishing between the intercessory power of night prayer recitation and the permanent record of deeds for daytime recitation. Scholarly tradition emphasizes the 'Qintar' (a massive weight of good deeds) as a metaphor for the overwhelming divine favor granted to those who engage deeply with the text, reinforcing the Shia emphasis on the Quran as both a guide and a source of eternal reward.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who recites one hundred Verses, praying Salāt with these during a night, Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic would Write for him, due to it, the Qunoot (supplication during Salāt) for a night;
and the one who recites two hundred Verses during other than a Salāt, the Quran would not argue against him on the Day of Judgment;

and the one who recites five hundred Verses during a day and a night during a Salāt of a day and a night, Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic would Write for him in the Guarded Tablet, a Qintar of good deeds,
and the Qintar is one thousand two hundred Owqiya, and the Owqiya is greater than the mountain of Ohad’.
en.sarwar: 9. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al- Hassan ibn Ali from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Whoever reads one hundred verses of the Holy Quran in prayer in the night, Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, will write down for him the reward for one night’s worshipping.
Whoever reads two hundred verses without being in prayer, the Holy Quran, on the Day of Judgment, will not argue against him.
Whoever reads five hundred verses in one day and night, Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, writes down for him in the protected tablet one Qintar of good deeds.
One Qintar is one thousand two hundred ‘Awqiyah, which is greater than the mountain of ‘Uhud.’”
